claim: For binary length-six single-deletion-correcting codes \(C\subseteq\{0,1\}^6\), the maximum cardinality is \(10\), and exactly nine labeled maximum codes attain it. Under the explicit order-four symmetry group generated by global bit complementation and word reversal, the nine maxima split into six orbits of sizes \(1,1,1,2,2,2\). Exactly one maximum is a Varshamov--Tenengolts syndrome class, namely \(VT_0(6)\); the other eight maxima are not VT classes. All nine maximum codes contain the common four-word core \(\{000000,001100,110011,111111\}\).

correctness.rationale: An exact stdlib verifier reconstructs the one-deletion compatibility graph on all 64 words and exhaustively enumerates every maximal clique via Bron--Kerbosch recursion with pivoting. It finds maximum 10 and exactly nine maxima, then directly checks every pairwise shadow disjointness condition, the stated order-four orbits, VT syndromes, and common core. Risk: implementation error is mitigated by direct post-enumeration checks but no independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete equality classification at a classical synchronization-code optimum. It distinguishes the known fact that VT_0(6) is optimal from the stronger false intuition that all optima are VT: eight of nine are non-VT, yet all share a fixed four-word core. This is structural information plausibly useful for understanding extremizer rigidity and near-VT constructions, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
